messages.text:
One useful finding: when output is captured, the reference suppresses all the progress/status `println` lines and leaves only the final elapsed/password lines for successful searches.

I’m switching to a small Python comparison harness now so stdout and stderr are separated exactly, including argument errors.

commands.commandLine:
"C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command "@'
import subprocess, pathlib, json, os
root=pathlib.Path.cwd()
ref=pathlib.Path(root/'REFERENCE_BINARY.txt').read_text().strip()
cases=[
  ['--version'],
  [],
  ['-i','nope.zip'],
  ['-i',str(root/'rust-reference/test-files/2.test.txt.zip'), '--workers','0'],
  ['-i',str(root/'rust-reference/test-files/2.test.txt.zip'), '--minPasswordLen','0'],
  ['-i',str(root/'rust-reference/test-files/2.test.txt.zip'), '--minPasswordLen','3','--maxPasswordLen','2'],
  ['-i',str(root/'rust-reference/test-files/2.test.txt.zip'), '--charset','x','--maxPasswordLen','1'],
  ['-i',str(root/'rust-reference/test-files/2.test.txt.zip'), '--mask','?z'],
  ['-i',str(root/'rust-reference/test-files/2.test.txt.zip'), '--customCharset1','abc'],
  ['-i',str(root/'rust-reference/test-files/2.test.txt.zip'), '-s','A','-c','l'],
]
for args in cases:
    p=subprocess.run([ref,*args], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True)
    print('CASE',args)
    print('code',p.returncode)
    print('stdout',repr(p.stdout))
    print('stderr',repr(p.stderr))
    print('---')
'@ | python -"
